page: Microsoft Azure E64d_v5 is a memory-optimized instance engineered for large memory footprints and local storage demands. It is powered by the Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 48 MB of L3 cache. Memory resources stand at 512.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a 2,577 GB SSD attached via Microsoft Hyper-V, and the instance includes zero dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate pronounced strengths in parallelized compute and memory operations. Multi-core performance is robust, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 62,154.25 and a PassMark CPU score of 60,539.43, both placing in the top quartile. Large-block memory bandwidth is similarly strong, delivering 298.57 GB/sec for uncached reads and 130.67 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific metrics show 62.33 million Redis SET operations per second and 54.92 GB/sec in static web throughput. Single-core processing across Geekbench (1,702.0) and stress-ng (1,899.18) ranks in the average range, reflecting standard per-core speeds.

The primary operational tradeoff relates to compute-bound single-thread workloads and unaccelerated artificial intelligence tasks. While smaller language models execute with acceptable throughput, large 70B model text generation drops to 2.71 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. With its extensive RAM capacity, fast multi-threaded execution, and included 2,577 GB SSD, the E64d_v5 delivers efficient resource density for relational enterprise databases, in-memory caches, software compilation, and large-scale data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64d_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud server equipped with 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores) on the Intel Xeon 8370C architecture operating at 2.8 GHz. It integrates 512.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, paired with 2,577 GB of local SSD storage. Evaluated benchmarks highlight top-tier multi-threaded processing, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 60,539.43, uncached read bandwidth of 298.57 GB/sec, and 62.33 million Redis SET operations per second. Single-core tests such as Geekbench single-core (1,702.0) fall within the median tier, and the absence of discrete GPUs limits large-scale model inference throughput. The architecture offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for dense enterprise workloads, making it well matched for in-memory databases, large caching clusters, distributed data analytics, and high-throughput static web serving.
